correctness.rationale: At a leg endpoint ai ei the tangent cone is {G_j≥0 for j≠i, G_i+Σ(ai/aj)G_j≤0}. For ai≥ak, interchanging Gaussian coordinate labels in the pk cone shows event inclusion; it is strict on an open set if ai>ak, and p0=2^-d>pi. At any longest leg L, write tj=aj/L≤1. Direct Gaussian change of variables on the cone yields p*/Q=(2π)^(-d/2)∫_{R_+^d}exp(−[(z0+Σzj)^2+Σtj² zj²]/2)dz, Q=∏tj. Replacing all tj by 1 lowers the integrand and gives C_d, equality precisely all legs equal; dropping Σtj² zj² gives strict U_d, and dominated convergence as all tj→0 proves sharpness. Simplex slice ∫_{positive orthant} f(Σz)=[1/(d−1)!]∫s^(d−1)f(s) gives U_d=Γ(d/2)/[2(d−1)!π^(d/2)]. d2 right-triangle angle and d3 classical trihedral formula give stated values and sharp degeneration; fixed other legs and L→∞ yields p*∼U_d∏others/L^(d−1) and Ωmin/(dμ)→1. Checked dimensions, normalization, equality cases and the existence of a strict gap for every nondegenerate shape; finite numerical checks are supplemental.

value.rationale: Vertex solid angles and fullness are standard meaningful simplex-quality measures in anisotropic meshing. The theorem supplies full rank-order rigidity and dimension-sharp uniform shape anisotropy coefficients, including exact equality and highly anisotropic degeneration, for the canonical right-simplex family. Unlike a raw trig substitution, the orthant integral comparison is all-dimensional and locates sharp constants.
residual_risks: Restriction to coordinate-orthogonal family prevents inferring the same coefficients for arbitrary simplices.

limitations: No claim for degenerate zero legs or arbitrary skew simplices.
The explicit trihedral-angle identity is not novel in isolation.
